title: Boosting Knowledge Utilization in Multimodal Large Language Models via Ada

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract states: 'Contradicting prior assumptions, ALFAR employs light training to optimize its fusion weights and attention reallocation parameters, which involve fine-tuning on selected benchmarks, thereby limiting its plug-and-play capability. As a plug-and-play method, ALFAR achieves superior performance across diverse datasets without requiring additional training or external tools.' This directly contradicts itself (light training vs. no additional training) and contradicts the rest of the paper, which repeatedly claims the method is training-free and plug-and-play.

The caption lists 'Vanilla LLaVA: Ground-truth knowledge 39.15'. However, Table 1 shows that LLaVA-1.5 without context (Parametric) achieves 39.15 on InfoSeek, while providing ground-truth knowledge should yield much higher accuracy. The bar labeled 'Ground-truth knowledge 39.15' is thus mislabeled; it most likely represents the no-context baseline, making the figure misleading.

The text claims the attention reallocation adjusts attention 'based on the retrieval similarity α in Eq. 1 … Specifically, less attention is allocated to image tokens if the context is more reliable with a high retrieval similarity.' However, the only equations for modifying attention—Eq. (6) and (7)—introduce a query-context relevance score ω_j and boost context tokens by (1+ k ω_j). No term involving α appears, and there is no explicit mechanism to reduce image token attention based on α. The described behaviour is not implemented by the given equations.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2, after Eq. (10) and the final fusion equation
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The final logits fusion is p(y_t) ~ softmax(λ_v^t · logit_p + λ_c^t · logit_c), and the text adds 'ensuring positive weights that sum to 1 to consistently balance parametric and contextual knowledge.' However, λ_v^t and λ_c^t are raw sums of attention weights over image and context tokens (Eq. 10) and are not normalized; their sum is generally less than 1 because attention is also distributed over query and other tokens. The stated property that the weights sum to 1 is therefore incorrect under the described formulas.

The equations in the paper are numbered (1), (2), (3), (4), then jump directly to (6) without an equation (5). The missing label creates a gap in the sequence and may indicate a removed or misplaced formula, causing a presentational defect.
